title: End-to-end Generate→Verify→Repair (GVR) for Intent-to-Configuration Safety — Repaired Preregistration
research_question: Does an end-to-end generate→verify→repair pipeline that integrates an LLM, a deterministic network verifier, and a network emulator materially reduce operational-safety violations in LLM-generated network configurations compared to LLM-only generation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: A GVR pipeline reduces the proportion of intents producing at least one safety-policy violation (verifier flag + emulator-confirmed) by ≥30 percentage points relative to LLM-only generation (paired within-intent comparison).
H2: Repairs produced by the GVR pipeline do not increase median emulator-observed configuration latency by more than 10% relative to the original LLM outputs (paired within-intent comparison).
exploratory_questions: E1: How many repair iterations are typically required per violated intent (distribution of repair iterations)?
E2: Which verifier-flag classes (reachability, ACL, loop/policy) are most amenable to automatic repair?
E3: Vendor-conditional effects: does GVR effectiveness vary by vendor CLI family (Cisco, Juniper, Arista)?
benchmark_scope: Publicly collectible NetOps natural-language intents (see Sampling Plan).
Emulator-only execution (Mininet-based topologies in docker containers).

Deterministic, rule-based verifier coverage limited to syntactic/semantic network properties expressible as reachability, ACL/ACL-order, loop/detected-forwarding-loop, and explicit policy contradictions as encoded in the verifier ruleset below.
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API selected and fixed for the confirmatory experiment (model identifier and exact API call settings pre-registered below).
All prompt templates and random-seed variants are pre-registered; no manual selection/annotation is permitted post-lock — automated scoring/picking rules are pre-registered.
transformation_scope: Text-to-configuration extraction (LLM output → normalized vendor CLI config) transformations are deterministic parsing scripts (regex + AST) run in CPU Docker containers.

Verifier reports converted to structured JSON error reports by deterministic parsers; repair prompts are constructed by deterministic templates that interpolate the JSON error report and the prior config.
primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in proportions of intents that produce at least one safety-policy violation (verifier flag that is confirmed as emulator-failure) between LLM-only and GVR-final configurations.
secondary_estimands: Paired median difference in emulator-observed TCP/ICMP latency proxy between LLM-only and GVR-final configs per intent.
Distribution of repair iterations per intent (mean, median, IQR).
Per-violation-type (reachability, ACL, loop/policy) absolute reduction in violation proportion.
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N = 100 unique natural-language NetOps intents. Stratified sampling by vendor-family: Cisco = 34, Juniper = 33, Arista = 33. Intent sourcing procedure (automated): crawl and collect public instructional task pages, open-source labs, vendor examples, and community-run NetOps problem lists (publicly accessible URLs) using deterministic scraping scripts; filter to remove duplicates and non-actionable intents with automated heuristics (intent must specify a concrete connectivity or policy objective). The final sampled set will be snapshot (URI list + hash) and published as the experiment intent corpus. Inclusion: English-language actionable intent with a reachable topology mapping; Exclusion: intents requiring proprietary devices or private data. Confirmatory_items = 100. Discovery_items = 0 (no unregistered exploratory sampling for confirmatory claims).
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired comparison of per-intent binary outcome (safety violation: yes/no) between LLM-only and GVR-final configs. Use McNemar exact test (two-sided, alpha=0.05) to test H1; report absolute and relative reduction with 95% bootstrap percentile CIs (10k bootstrap iterations). For latency (H2) compute paired differences in median latency proxies across intents and use Wilcoxon signed-rank test (two-sided, alpha=0.05); report median ratio and 95% CI via bootstrap. Pre-register subgroup (vendor) analyses; apply Bonferroni correction across the 3 vendor subgroup tests for primary estimand. Report all raw counts, discordant-pair tables, effect sizes, and per-intent artifacts. All code for analysis is deterministic and will be published (Docker + seed).
multiplicity_plan: Primary familywise alpha reserved for H1 only. Secondary estimands and subgroup tests are exploratory or multiplicity-corrected as follows: per-vendor tests (3) use Bonferroni correction (alpha_adj = 0.05/3). All other secondary analyses are reported with nominal p-values and flagged as exploratory.
missingness_plan: If any intent execution (LLM call or emulator run) fails due to infrastructure error, the failure is logged and an automated retry policy applies: up to 2 automated re-executions (same seed/config) for infrastructure faults only. If after retries the artifact is still unavailable, the intent is excluded from confirmatory paired analysis and counted in a missingness table; a sensitivity analysis (complete-case vs. worst-case imputation where missing baseline = violation, missing GVR = non-violation and vice versa) will be reported. All exclusions and their deterministic automated failure reasons will be published.

benchmark_names: Public NetOps Intent Corpus (snapshot URIs published at time of run)
risk_factors: Intent corpus overlap with LLM training data (model vendor nondeterminism).
Repeated prompting that could lead to implicit memorization or leakage between runs.
External web-retrieval used in prompts (none used in confirmatory protocol).
detection_procedures: Record and publish all prompt text and LLM responses; perform automated substring checks to detect verbatim matches with any sampled intent text (flag possible leakage).
Log per-call deterministic hashes and compare duplicates across seeds/templates to detect cross-run contamination.
item_flagging_rules: Flag an intent as 'potentially contaminated' if any LLM response includes a >80-character verbatim span that matches any source URI content in the intent corpus snapshot.
Flag repeated identical outputs across different seeds/templates as 'duplicate-output' for downstream sensitivity checks.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analyses exclude flagged contaminated items from confirmatory inference (pre-registered conservative approach). Secondary analyses include contaminated items with explicit labeling. All flagged items are published with redaction as required by the artifact sharing policy.
residual_uncertainty: Residual uncertainty remains about model pretraining overlaps with public examples outside the captured snapshot; classified as noncritical external-validity limitation.

budget_scenarios.description: Balanced feasible run (recommended). N=100 intents, 3 prompt templates × 2 random seeds = 6 initial LLM calls per intent; deterministic automated selection uses the verifier pass-rate and a simple lexical score to pick the baseline config. GVR repair: verifier-triggered repairs allowed up to 3 iterations; expected average repair iterations per intent = 1.5 among violating intents. Emulation and verification run in Docker containers on CPU. Total confirmatory_items = 100, task_cluster_count = 3 (Cisco/Juniper/Arista).
models: single hosted LLM API (model-identifier to be fixed at freeze; API calls counted as planned_model_calls)
transformations: 3 prompt templates × 2 seeds per intent (initial generation), deterministic parsing to vendor CLI AST, repair-prompt templates (one LLM call per repair iteration).
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Planned_model_calls 750 derived as: 100 intents × 6 initial calls = 600 initial calls; expected average repairs = 0.6 calls/intent (100 × 0.6 = 60); overhead for retries/logging ≈ 90 calls; total ≈ 750. This fits the capability manifest (maximum_planned_model_calls 10000) and can run within the 7‑day wall clock using CPU Docker containers and hosted model API quotas.

budget_scenarios.description: Higher-power, higher-cost run. N=150 intents, 5 prompt templates × 3 seeds = 15 initial LLM calls per intent; repairs up to 3 iterations; deeper logging and larger bootstrap (10k) retained. task_cluster_count = 3.
models: single hosted LLM API (model-identifier to be fixed at freeze)
transformations: 5 prompt templates × 3 seeds per intent initial generation; deterministic parsing and repair prompting up to 3 iterations
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Planned_model_calls 2400 derived as: 150 intents × 15 initial = 2250 initial calls; expected repairs ~150 × 0.45 baseline-violation-rate × 1.0 avg repairs ≈ 68 repairs; overhead ≈ 82 calls; total ≈ 2400. This remains within the model-call budget in the capability manifest but requires larger run-time and is not the recommended primary scenario due to cost/time.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in per-intent violation proportion (LLM-only vs GVR-final).
power_plan.target_effect: Absolute reduction of 30 percentage points (e.g., from 40% baseline to 10% after GVR).
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate paired McNemar power calculation using assumed baseline violation rate p1=0.40 and post-GVR p2=0.10. Discordant-pair proportion estimated as p1*(1-p2)+p2*(1-p1)=0.42. Using N=100, expected discordant count ≈ 42; approximate power (asymptotic normal approximation + continuity correction) ≈ 0.85. We will report exact McNemar p-values and bootstrap CIs in final analysis.
assumptions: Baseline violation rate (LLM-only) ≈ 40% (conservative estimate from domain extrapolation).
Post-GVR violation rate target = 10% (≥30pp absolute reduction).
No more than 10% of intents will be lost to unrecoverable infrastructure failures (handled in missingness_plan).
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=100 and the above baseline assumption, the analysis has ~85% power to detect a 30pp absolute reduction; if baseline violation rate is lower (<30%), detectable absolute reductions will be smaller (power falls). Sensitivity analyses will report power across baseline rates 25%–50%.
sensitivity_analyses: Power recalculated for baseline p1 in {0.25,0.35,0.45}.
Bootstrap-based 95% CIs for paired proportion difference (10k resamples).

transformation_families: Text → vendor CLI normalization (regex-based parser → AST).
Verifier JSON report → repair-prompt template interpolation.
Emulator test-suite scripts (topology template → deterministic tests for reachability/ACL/loop).
semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip check: parsed AST → canonicalized CLI → re-parse and compare AST equality; mismatches rejected automatically.
Verifier-consistency check: if verifier flags no violations but emulator test fails, mark item as 'verifier-emulator discordant' and include in sensitivity analyses.
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject and re-run any LLM output that fails deterministic CLI parsing (parser error) up to retry policy (2 retries) — failure after retries becomes recorded infrastructure or generation failure and is handled per missingness_plan.
Reject any parsed config that contains syntactically disallowed commands as defined in the pre-registered forbidden-commands list (to avoid emulator breakage).
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: Automated deterministic audit sample: publish full parsed ASTs and verifier logs for 20% randomly selected intents (seeded RNG) for external reproducibility; all artifacts are hashed and published. No manual annotation or adjudication will be used.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Mapping from verifier-flag types to emulator test suite is pre-registered: (1) reachability flag → ICMP/TCP connectivity checks between specified endpoints in the Mininet topology; (2) ACL violation → packet-drop expectation tests; (3) loop/policy → traceroute/forwarding-path checks for persistent forwarding loops. Mappings are deterministic and implemented as test scripts.
residual_risks: Verifier rule blind spots for high-level intent misinterpretation (semantic policy divergence) remain; emulator confirmation reduces but does not eliminate this risk.
Emulator-simulator mismatch to real vendor hardware behavior is a noncritical external-validity limitation.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Emulator fidelity: Mininet-based emulation may not reproduce vendor-specific hardware idiosyncrasies; this limits external generalizability but does not prevent testing the paired hypotheses within the declared emulator scope.

Verifier coverage: deterministic verifier ruleset cannot capture all semantic/policy interpretation errors; residual unsafe constructs may remain undetected but emulator confirmation mitigates many such cases.
Potential overlap between public intent corpus samples and LLM pretraining data (contamination flagging and exclusion mitigate this risk; residual uncertainty remains).
Single-model scope: inferences apply only to the tested hosted-model API; generalization to other LLMs is noncritical and explicitly out of scope for confirmatory claims.
